title: Total positivity of Fuss–Narayana triangles and strict positivity of their squares
statement:
For an integer $m\geq 1$ and $n\geq k\geq 0$, define

$$
FNA_{\langle m\rangle}(n,k)=\frac{1}{n+1}\binom{n+1}{k}\binom{m(n+1)}{n-k},\qquad FNB_{\langle m\rangle}(n,k)=\binom{n}{k}\binom{mn}{n-k}.
$$

Let $FN_{A,\langle m\rangle}$ and $\overleftarrow{FN}_{A,\langle m\rangle}$ be the corresponding type-$A$ Fuss–Narayana triangles, and let $FN_{B,\langle m\rangle}$ and $\overleftarrow{FN}_{B,\langle m\rangle}$ be the corresponding type-$B$ triangles; define the associated Fuss–Narayana squares by

$$
FN_{A,\langle m\rangle}^{\ulcorner}=\left[FNA_{\langle m\rangle}(n+k,k)\right]_{n,k\geq 0},\qquad FN_{B,\langle m\rangle}^{\ulcorner}=\left[FNB_{\langle m\rangle}(n+k,k)\right]_{n,k\geq 0}.
$$

**Fuss–Narayana conjecture.** For any $m\geq 1$, the Fuss–Narayana triangles are totally positive and the Fuss–Narayana squares are strictly totally positive. The source introduces this as a proposed conjecture, and no resolution is supplied.
source_name: Yi Wang and Arthur L. B. Yang, “Total positivity of Narayana matrices”, arXiv:1702.07822 (2017).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07822

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).
